title: skills: ship /github-weekly, source roster from Notion, auto-extend Week
author: jeremyconner1975
head: 222aa3ab198c9fd03a7a6ea1b2f9b1fb590e9ed7
body:
## Summary

Three closely-related drift fixes for the team skills:

1. **Add `/github-weekly` as a shared skill.** PR #5 made `/weekly-progress` call `/github-weekly`, but `/github-weekly` was never committed to this repo — it lived only as a personal command on one machine. Anyone other than the original author hits a dangling reference after `./install.sh`.

2. **Source the team roster from Notion.** Replace the hardcoded 9-row roster tables in `/weekly-progress` and `/github-weekly` with a runtime lookup against the [Accelerator Platform Software](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/Accelerator-Platform-Software-31fd132d3cfd80a1af67de154a08451a) Notion page, with GitHub handles resolved by querying the `aps` GitHub team. One source of truth — the page is what changes when the team changes.

3. **Auto-extend the Stories DB `Week` dropdown.** Adds a step to `/weekly-progress` (Step 0.5) and `/flow-create` (Step 1.5) that ensures the current week's option exists in the Stories DB `Week` select, auto-extending 8 weeks ahead via `notion-update-data-source` if not. Fixes the "Week dropdown only goes to W18" symptom Jesse flagged today; the dropdown self-maintains from now on.

## Why

The check-in flow had three accumulating sources of drift:
- A skill referenced from another skill but not shipped (#1)
- Two hand-maintained rosters that diverged any time the team changed (#2)
- A Notion select that needed manual extension every quarter and silently broke things when forgotten (#3)

This PR collapses each into a single canonical source.

## Changes

- `skills/github-weekly/SKILL.md` (new) — frontmatter follows team-skill convention; roster reads from Notion at run time; output is inline by default with optional file save.
- `skills/weekly-progress/SKILL.md` — Step 0.5 ensures current Week exists; Team Roster section replaced with Notion-page reference.
- `skills/flow-create/SKILL.md` — Step 1.5 ensures current Week exists when the user is setting Week.
- `install.sh` — install the new skill.
- `README.md` — document the new skill.
- (Out of band, not in this diff) the Stories DB `Week` select was extended to W26 (Jun 23) to unblock today's W19 work.

## Test plan

- [ ] `./install.sh` reports four skills installed
- [ ] `/github-weekly` standalone produces an inline 7-day report; team roster reflects the Notion page
- [ ] `/weekly-progress` Step 0.5 is a no-op now that W19 exists; deleting and re-running auto-recreates if removed
- [ ] `/weekly-progress --all` runs end-to-end with the new GitHub Activity section
- [ ] `/flow-create` setting Week on a story works without manual dropdown maintenance

title: Add native numerical validation for Qwen3.5 MoE inference
author: positron-jessezhang
head: 927d501a8648b53cdaafff22e7a82107c980a337
body:
Add independent numerical checks for standalone Qwen3.5 MoE text inference.

## Problem

Running the full model exposed GDN buffers being overwritten before their final use, incorrect shared-gate tensor layout, and SAL scalar precision mismatches. Generated tokens alone did not establish numerical correctness.

## Solution

Preserve live GDN buffers, correct tensor loading and scalar precision, and add an independent reference with strict checkpoint comparisons for each generation step. Add a 256-expert/top-8 tiny case covering prefill and two decode steps, supported by synthetic GDN regressions and reusable validation artifacts. Mark only the three native-oracle tests whose provenance checks require the RTL checkout. The frozen tiny checkpoint digest is registered in `docs/ANCHORED_EVIDENCE.md` with its provenance in `docs/QWEN35_MOE_NATIVE_VALIDATION.md`. A review pass then consolidated the tolerance rule, margin constants, row-position derivation and comparison-JSON writes into single owners, gated capture-mode recording consistently, restored the conservative scratch reservation for undeclared GDN geometry, and made the reference refuse an undeclared head layout for grouped heads; frozen reference arithmetic and the suite's embedded checkpoint names were left unchanged.

## Testing

- On this head (rebased onto current main, RTL present): nearest and merged test files 753 passed, 0 failed; contract lane 111 passed; light gate all six lanes green (src 801 passed / 7 skipped, 12321 tests collected); tiny canonical passed (prefill plus two decode steps, tokens and all checkpoint gates); `tools.prime_radiant check` and `asim validation hf-survey reports --check` pass; the tiny fixture regenerated before and after the review fixes is byte-identical except the oracle's provenance hashes of the edited reference sources.
- The first full validation of the review pass caught a regression the light gate cannot see: a leftover function-local import in the MoE expert path raised `UnboundLocalError` whenever checkpoint capture was on (tiny canonical and four MoE external-oracle cases failed). Fixed in this head; those five cases pass again. No arithmetic changed.
- Same runtime arithmetic on the pre-rebase head 3e71b6c4: full gate red only on lanes this branch does not own (Gemma strict logits, a C2C ledger check needing Python 3.12.3, Prime Radiant witnesses needing Verilator); tiny canonical passed; two fresh real 35B runs produced ` Paris.\n` through all 40 layers with 0 mismatches against the frozen 3,574-gate suite, and their exact repeat comparison found 0 differences across 4,174 checkpoints.
- A static guard (`tests/test_import_shadowing_guard.py`) now pins that mechanism: a function-scope use of a module-level imported name must not precede a local import of it. Zero hits across `src/asim`, `tests`, `tools`, `scripts`; against the regressed file it reports both crash sites.
- The full validation restarted on the rebased head got through contract, Prime Radiant check, src and the bulk lane (bulk: only the two known non-owned failures, Gemma and the C2C Python-version check) before it was stopped to fold the guard and merge; the 35B acceptance and repeat therefore stand on the earlier head with identical runtime arithmetic (see above), not on this exact head.
commit_subjects: feat(validation): qualify Qwen3.5 MoE with native numerical gates

Good catch: it was not registered. title: AGENTS.md: choose the gate by what a change can alter, not by its breadth
author: bihe-positron
head: 3dcdd4119629720b6d8ed0b1774d12ae5505bc62
body:
## Summary

AGENTS.md section 2 chose between `--fast` and the full gate by the breadth of a change ("large in behavior ... across subsystems"). A change touching the bridge, the attention runtime and V-offset layout read as cross-subsystem and required the full gate, whose wall time is the canonical lane's longest case (the lane already runs its cases concurrently; `--jobs` beyond the case count does not shorten it). A change inside one subsystem that could move a token needed only `--fast`, whose lanes run synthetic weights and never execute the canonical default suite.

This PR makes the gate choice follow what a change can alter:

- **Step 3** — `--fast` is the whole requirement only for a change that cannot alter a produced token or the structural audit's record and does not trigger the full gate; a timing or scheduling change that moves when a value is produced, consumed or retired can alter either; uncertainty means the canonical tier.
- **Step 4, canonical tier** — any change that can alter a token or the audit's record: `--fast` plus the canonical default suite, run to completion on the exact tree pushed; `--case` and `--smoke` are prechecks. One exception to the pre-push rule: a canonical run started on the pushed tree before push may still be running at push, recorded as pending (section 8) and completed, passing, before merge; a failure after push is a section 3 report.
- **Step 4, full gate** — a rebaseline or any change to the executable canonical verification contract. Cross-subsystem breadth alone no longer requires full. "Apply the strongest match" keeps full precedence.

Owner decisions (2026-10-02): adopt the breadth relaxation; adopt the pending-at-push exception for the canonical tier only; do not move any canonical case to nightly.

## Same-PR synchronisation

- `scripts/pre_merge_gate.sh` header: full-mode note rewritten; it now also lists the files that make up the executable canonical verification contract and what full adds over `--fast` + the canonical suite (slow serial, slow Prime Radiant, mandatory llama.cpp crosscheck).
- `scripts/hooks/pre-push` comment: no longer says "before merging a rebaseline/large change"; points at section 2 step 4 and the gate header.
- `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`: items 3 and 4 follow the new steps; the Canonical status section carries the per-tier completion rules and the "unmergeable until a rerun passes" consequence.
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md`: the canonical table row and the two paragraphs that described the old "large change" rule now defer to section 2 step 4; the smoke paragraph adds the named-case precheck and says why the suite's elapsed time is roughly its slowest case; the `--jobs 8` literal is removed from the edited example (the runner's default runs every selected case concurrently).

## Intentional decisions

- The sentence "Run independent long canonical jobs in parallel, not serially" is dropped: the runner's default (`--jobs 0`) runs all selected cases concurrently, so for the default suite the instruction is redundant; it was efficiency guidance, not a gate requirement.
- "canonical change" (previously undefined) is written as "any change to the executable canonical verification contract" with the file list in the gate header; a change that alters canonical *results* is the canonical tier, not full. If the old wording was meant to cover result-changing code, this is a third relaxation; recorded here rather than left implicit.
- Measured per-case durations are not recorded in docs (they move with host and pin); the docs say only that elapsed time is bounded by the slowest case.
- AGENTS.md stays under the contract test's 24,576-byte cap (24,545 after this change); the cap is not raised.

## Validation

Tree: this branch at its head. `tests/test_agent_contract.py` + `tools/doc_checks/` + `tests/test_lane_topology.py` + `tests/test_hf_report_artifacts.py` (it pins QUICKSTART/README phrases; the first CI run caught the one this PR had reworded, now restored) + `tests/test_driver_facade_surface.py` + `tests/test_bf19_pai_reference.py`: 328 passed, 55 skipped, 3 deselected — the three `test_rust_gate_selects_reviewed_benchmark_and_propagates_failures` cases fail identically on an unmodified origin/main checkout when run from a worktree without its own `.venv` (the rust lane returns before the stubbed cargo is reached), so they are environmental; they pass on a checkout with a venv. `bash -n` on the two edited shell files. No lane command, selector or pyproject text changes, so the lane-topology contract is unaffected (its tests pass above).

Reviews: the rule text went through four rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max and three zero-context Claude reviews (plan side); the diff went through three blind rounds with gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (last round A0 B0 C0) and two blind zero-context Claude reviews (last round A0; its B/C items — hook text, the `--jobs 8` literal, intro wording, the post-push failure consequence — are applied in the final commit).

## Review follow-ups (after the first ready)

- Codex P1 ×3: the gate header's contract list is marked non-exhaustive and gains the `.tron` artifact modules; the canonical tier requires the opt-in cases or suite for each model, execution mode or feature path the change reaches that the default suite does not exercise (if none exists, the PR says so and gets the user's go-ahead); step 4 no longer says full contains the canonical tier — full replaces `--fast` and the default-suite run, supplemental runs still apply. The executable contract is defined by responsibility (case selection, artifact construction, orchestration, acceptance checks) with the file list in the gate header; the pending-at-push exception is scoped to canonical runs and written per required run in the PR template.
- Blind reviews of the follow-up diff: gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max (two rounds, last A0 B0 after one wording fix) and zero-context Claude (A0; its remaining B/C: the dropped "run canonical jobs in parallel" sentence is recorded above as intentional; dependency/toolchain pin bumps are covered by "can alter a produced token" but not named in the examples — follow-up; `README.md:373` and `docs/QUICKSTART.md:806` keep a `--jobs 8` literal — pre-existing, follow-up).

## Owner decision after the first ready (2026-10-05)

The first wording of step 3 ("timing or scheduling changes can alter either; when in doubt, run the canonical tier") would have moved seven of the last two weeks' merged single-subsystem fixes from `--fast` into the canonical tier without catching anything. Step 3 now decides by whether the change can alter a produced token or the structural-audit verdict (violation count, required events) on a reachable path (from an `asim` command or the canonical runner, not test-only hooks); a timing change that reorders a value's production, consumption or retirement can; when in doubt the author asks the user and records the answer under item 4 of the PR template. Step 4 carries the same qualifiers. Reviews of this wording: gpt-6-astra at thinking_mode max two rounds (last A0 B0 C0), zero-context Claude two rounds (last A0; its B/C residuals are listed below as follow-ups).

## Known residuals (recorded, not changed here)

- A rebaseline's "supplemental runs" set is not spelled out in step 4; `docs/RTL_REBASELINE_GUIDE.md` governs rebaseline coverage and should name it when that guide is next touched.
- "(violation count, required events)" summarises the runner's structural-audit judgement; the runner also checks required-event counts and metadata and parses the report — a change that alters those without changing the verdict class should be treated as changing the verdict.
- Opt-in IR and tiny-validation cases judge more than tokens and the structural audit (IR runtime dumps, execution packages); a change that alters only those outputs is not pulled into the canonical tier by the text — intentional narrowing for now.
- The commit body keeps the canonical status it had at push; the PR template's Canonical status section carries the completion.
- AGENTS.md sits 9 bytes under the contract cap; the §7 marker descriptions are reference material that a separate cleanup PR should move to docs/ to restore headroom.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `README.md:373` and `docs/QUICKSTART.md:806` still show `--jobs 8` in command examples (pre-existing).
- Name dependency/toolchain pin bumps (numerics libraries, the Rust toolchain) among the canonical-tier examples once the byte budget allows (today 4 bytes of headroom).
- Installed hooks are copies; `scripts/install_hooks.sh` refreshes the comment text.
- `docs/canonical_results/README.md:14-15` advises choosing `--jobs` for the machine; consistent with the rule (any `--jobs` satisfies the tier), kept as is.

title: busybox: enable taskset for core pinning
author: positron-jessezhang
head: 19d87a9f4a4ed962fd1fd140c933b726d28bd669
body:
Enables the busybox `taskset` applet in the Asimov rootfs.

**Problem:** The rootfs shipped without `taskset`, so there was no way to pin a process to a specific CPU core.

**Solution:** Turn on `CONFIG_TASKSET` in the board busybox config, plus `FEATURE_TASKSET_FANCY` + `FEATURE_TASKSET_CPULIST` so the `-c` cpu-list form works (`taskset -c 3 ./app`). `-c` depends on FANCY in busybox kconfig, so all three are needed; this matches busybox upstream defaults.

**Testing:** Built busybox from this config and ran it natively — applet present in `--list`, `--help` shows the `-c LIST` form, `/usr/bin/taskset` lands in busybox.links, and `taskset -c 0 … -c -p` pins to core 0 and reads the affinity list back.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Config-only change that adds a standard BusyBox utility; no auth, data, or runtime logic is modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> The Asimov rootfs **busybox** build config now ships the **`taskset`** applet so processes can be pinned to specific CPU cores on the device.
> 
> **`CONFIG_TASKSET`**, **`CONFIG_FEATURE_TASKSET_FANCY`**, and **`CONFIG_FEATURE_TASKSET_CPULIST`** are turned on in `br2-external/board/asimov/busybox.config`, enabling the **`-c` cpu-list** form (e.g. `taskset -c 3 ./app`). FANCY is required for `-c` in BusyBox kconfig; this matches typical upstream defaults.
> 
> No other files change—**`asimov_defconfig`** already points at this busybox config, so the next image build picks up **`/usr/bin/taskset`** via the usual busybox symlinks.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 19d87a9f4a4ed962fd1fd140c933b726d28bd669. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: boot-fvp: never pre-arm telnet in headless runs; tell the truth about the console
author: bihe-positron
head: f890f77a271a081200d3ee602d53c70bb539c114
body:
An armed TelnetTerminal with no reading client back-pressures its UART after 16 KiB and the guest busy-spins on `UARTFR.TXFF` — a boot that "hangs" with the UART log frozen at exactly 16383 bytes, last line truncated mid-word. Headless runs with `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1` (the combo DEVELOPMENT.md itself recommended for a live AP console) hit this a few seconds after the script exits at the boot marker; in bridge mode (userspace marker, past 16 KiB) such runs always timed out at 124 with the FVP left wedged. This is the "headless boot hang" from the Terminus+Asim thread.

The fix rides on a component fact: the telnet listener is bound regardless of `start_telnet`, so pre-arming a terminal in a headless run buys nothing — the console stays attachable either way — while costing the wedge.

## Changes

- **headless launches always pass `start_telnet=0` to the model** (`MODEL_TELNET`); `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1 --headless` can no longer wedge a boot
- **`bp.terminal_0` is never pre-armed** (interactive included): the script only ever attaches a client to `ap_terminal`, and the BP UART carries no console output — an armed, undrained terminal there was the same trap waiting
- interactive mode unchanged in behavior: `ap_terminal` keeps `=1` and the script attaches its own client immediately
- the headless success message replaces the misleading "Telnet disabled. Re-run with ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1" (the port is open regardless) with the real contract: console log path, attach-anytime `telnet localhost <port>`, and the keep-reading caveat
- the timeout path hints at the one remaining stall cause — a client that attached earlier and disconnected/stopped draining — with the resolved port to reattach
- headless startup banner lists AP/BP/SCP UART logs explicitly (AP is the boot-marker + console log; it used to print only the output-less BP log). In passing, same class: the timeout `Check: tail -f` now points at the AP UART log, and the usage comment names `fvp-ap-uart-5.log`
- `DEVELOPMENT.md` knob row rewritten to match

## Verification (farm, this branch)

- trigger scenario A/B: `ASIMOV_ENABLE_TELNET=1 --headless` wedged at exactly 16383 bytes on the old script every time; with this fix it boots through to userspace (43K+ uart log)
- success path: boot to marker in 10.2s, new banner + Console/Attach messages print with the resolved port
- recovery claim: a deliberately wedged run was drained by attaching a reading client — log resumed 16383 → 43312 bytes, boot completed (what the hints promise)
- baseline: 45/45 headless boots (plain / BridgeFwd / BridgeFwd+asim) on the telnet-off path

## Remaining / out of scope

title: spec v0.1.4: Silver/Gold split, Figure 5 on Gold ABI v2, PR #118 counter-model note
author: jeremyconner1975
head: 3b1f9ae87bb91e0a763cfaa2190d12b5442d8692
body:
Brings the Asimov SW Architecture Spec current with the Silver/Gold work in `asimov-sw`. Every in-review citation carries its PR number and is labeled as pending merge + Interface-Spec confirmation; nothing unmerged is stated as settled.

## What's in it
- **§9 + §2 glossary: the Silver / Gold split** (per asimov-sw [#152](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/152), in review): Silver = the command language of the abstract machine, authored/verified in Lean, no loops/branches, one-hemisphere scope; Gold = the instruction language the C1-Nano decodes; certified resolution + lowering translates 1:1. Explicit statement that production placement is unchanged (Phoenix generates, C1 executes) and that [#169](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/169)'s Silver interpreter is a host-side *verification* model, not an execution venue.
- **§9.1 authority chain updated**: executing authority today = Gold ABI v2 (`asimov-interpreter` main, pinned to asimov-sw `8808746`, v1 rejected); successor normative docs = `silver-language.md` + `gold-abi.md` with Lean modules as canonical syntax (`Cmd` = Silver, `Insn` = Gold). The Haskell model / GOLD_V1 encoding doc are no longer the stated authority.
- **§9.1 delivery vocabulary**: environment image (per-pass, no `.program` entries), `fwd_pass_plan` demoted to a private runtime materialization, out-of-band program publication (THUNK→PROGRAM magic handshake), future CBOR compiler-artifact bundle — with the **dangling `compiler-artifact-cbor.md` reference flagged**.
- **Figure 5 + §9.2 redrawn to ABI v2** (closes the v0.1.3 §16 row): 28 instructions (5 fused SPA + 23 direct), one trusted mode with admission-then-abort, erased binding classes with slot 0 unbound, depth-8 calls with legal cycles (no cycle detection), `FAIL` as the only execution fault, `runtime/moe` layer beside the interpreter.
- **§13.2 counter-model NOTE** (asimov-sw [#118](https://github.com/positron-ai/asimov-sw/pull/118), changes-requested): 19-bit internal / 16- and 32-bit published windows, N−1 predecessor thresholds with strict wrap-aware compare, CPS/SAL divergence at 2^18, C2C tx/rx asymmetry, per-counter visibility limits. Flags §13.2's current numbers as superseded-pending-merge; wholesale rewrite waits for #118.
- **§16 rows updated**: encoding shape decided (16-bit tag + statically-known variable payload); family-rename follow-up gated on the Silver stack (#113 gates; #117 approved); new row for the unfinished compiler-artifact/loader path.

## Sequencing notes
- The §9.1 command-family list keeps v0.1 names with a rename NOTE — the rewrite to the Silver `Cmd` inventory waits for #117–#125 to merge.
- No overlap with #45/#58 (§14/observability) — this PR doesn't touch §14.

title: model: one C1-SME2 (CME) per cluster (NUM_CMES=1), matching the RTL pin
author: dmcdermott-positron
head: ef00e758e7185a7c9303e5b1d0592dc0e2fb22d7
body:
Story: [STORY-364 — Add SME2/VPU power domain support (C1-DSU)](https://www.notion.so/342d132d3cfd812bb78edd98d15249c7)

## What

The pinned RTL (`941a309cb`) builds one C1-SME2 unit (CME, Arm codename griffin) into every C1-DSU cluster — `C1_DSU_DynamIQ_Cluster_1.yaml` `NUM_CME: 1`, `griffin0_core u_cme_0` instantiated in the cluster wrapper, and the Nevis ID registers advertise SME2 unconditionally (`ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME=0b0010`, `ID_AA64SMFR0_EL1.SMEver=SME2`). The FVP's `NUM_CMES=0` default was therefore a silicon divergence: no SME on the model where silicon has it.

- Set `NUM_CMES=1` and the RTL-matched `DSU.cme.CMECFR` (ECC=1 from `CORE_CACHE_PROTECTION: TRUE`, CHI=0 from `NUM_COMPLEX_CHI: 1`) via `".default"` assignments on all five cluster instantiations. The per-cluster parameters stay live and init-time overridable (`-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=0` gives a CME-less A/B run).
- Keep `DSU.cme.power_on_by_default=true`: the Fast Models CME PPU registers are accepted but inert, so auto power-on stands in for the SCP's real CME-PPU dynamic-mode programming.
- Document the model limitations as **DD-12** (inert CME PPU at utility-bus `+0x280000`, unmodeled CME PPU IRQ/RAS/arbitration, partial CMECFR fidelity) and the decision as design-log **D-30**.

## FM 11.30 pitfall (why `".default"` and not the `NUM_CORES` binding pattern)

Delivering `NUM_CMES` through a top-level `PARAMETER` value binding kills every simulation at elaboration with `FATAL ERROR: An SMCU is implemented but FEAT_SME is not configured` — the binding fixes the sub-parameter out of the CADI store and the core model's internal FEAT_SME configuration never sees it. The same value applied as `-C cluster0.NUM_CMES=1`, or via `".default"` assignments (the semihosting-parameter idiom), works. Bisected against pristine main and the pinned fvp-v0.18.0; CMECFR content/escaping was ruled out. Recorded in D-30.

## Verified

- `make build` clean; `tests/run-all` **6/6** on the CME-enabled model; `cluster0..4.NUM_CMES=1` + CMECFR live in `--list-params`.
- Full asimov-os Linux boot on this model (with an SME-enabled BL31, asimov-tfa#33): userspace reached; SVE VL 128-bit, SME streaming VL 512-bit; no `sveaes/svepmull` (crypto ext fused off in RTL). `/proc/cpuinfo` from the booted system (both cores identical):

  ```
  processor       : 0
  BogoMIPS        : 2000.00
  Features        : fp asimd evtstrm crc32 atomics fphp asimdhp cpuid asimdrdm jscvt fcma lrcpc dcpop asimddp sve asimdfhm dit uscat ilrcpc flagm ssbs sb dcpodp sve2 svebitperm flagm2 frint svei8mm svebf16 i8mm bf16 dgh bti ecv afp sme smei8i32 smef16f32 smeb16f32 smef32f32 wfxt rprfm sme2 smei16i32 smebi32i32 mops hbc lrcpc3
  CPU implementer : 0x41
  CPU architecture: 8
  CPU variant     : 0x0
  CPU part        : 0xd8a
  CPU revision    : 0
  ```
- SCP firmware pytest suite: 42 passed / 16 skipped against this model.

## Consumer ordering

An SME-advertising model is only bootable behind a BL31 built with `ENABLE_SME_FOR_NS=2` (positron-ai/asimov-tfa#33): Linux writes `SMCR_EL2` at EL2 init whenever `ID_AA64PFR1_EL1.SME != 0`, and the current tfa-v0.6.0 BL31 dies silently right after its banner on this model (verified). Downstream pin bumps should take the SME-enabled asimov-tfa release before or together with the terminus release carrying this change.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UqQuy9BCy8ER19zmCu87JP

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Advertises SME2 on all AP cores and tightens boot ordering with TF-A; CME power sequencing still cannot be validated on the FVP (DD-13), so silicon-only regressions remain possible.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns the FVP with pinned RTL by giving all five `ARMC1NanoCT` clusters **one C1-SME2 (CME)** each: `NUM_CMES=1` and RTL-matched `DSU.cme.CMECFR` (ECC=1, CHI=0), applied via `".default"` so Fast Models still configures FEAT_SME and `-C clusterN.NUM_CMES=0` remains possible.
> 
> **DD-13** and design-log **D-30** document the decision, the FM 11.30 pitfall (top-level `PARAMETER` binding breaks SME elaboration), and remaining model gaps (inert CME PPU, unwired RAS IRQs, no core arbitration).
> 
> Downstream stacks need an SME-enabled BL31 (`ENABLE_SME_FOR_NS`) before or with this model release; otherwise Linux’s `SMCR_EL2` init traps at EL3.
>

Just for my own clarity: the way I understood our conversation on this, the goal is to (e.g.) be able to DMA-xfer a large block of data which may span _many_ descriptors, but only rely on completion/notification of the _last_ descriptor in the list.

title: Add observer hooks for save_k/save_v in model::state
author: bham0n
head: 6e81e4f27bd5c8088b8b4a257795c511a4c861ec
body:
In preparation for hw-kv-token-tree changes, which will intercept the calls to `save_v` and `save_k` independently, I'm introducing two Observer-pattern hook points: `on_save_k` and `on_save_v`. The parameters being used for calling this hook point will be unchanged, and will be identical to those currently taken by `save_k_to_hardware` and `save_v_to_hardware`.

Registering callbacks must be done before any prompting or generation with a model, to avoid concurrency issues. Here, the registration happens in the model::state constructor, which is guaranteed to be completed before a scheduler can use the model. 

There is one behavioral change. Page write is reordered before observer notification. With this change, the planned GOF readiness observer can find page data already written when it fires. This will not cause any additional latency for the code on the hwattention_sync branch, because both the DMA block and page write calls are blocking. Reversing the order won't affect the total per-token timing.

Implementing these hook points in this way will avoid (as much as possible) merge conflicts between `hamon-hktt-dma` (where hw-kv-token-tree DMA changes are being developed) and `hwattention_sync`. 

Additionally, `make format` identified a number of minor formatting fixes in device.hpp and t_hwattention.cpp 


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the KV-save call path and ordering around page writes vs DMA notification, which can affect correctness/timing for hardware attention and any future observers; concurrency expectations depend on observers being registered before inference starts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **observer-style hook points** in `model::state` (`on_save_k` and `on_save_v`) to allow multiple callbacks to be invoked when KV data is saved, while registering the existing `tron::hardware::save_k_to_hardware` / `save_v_to_hardware` as the default observers.
> 
> Updates `save_k`/`save_v` to **write KV data into the page first**, then collect per-head pointers and notify all registered observers instead of calling the hardware save functions directly. Also includes minor `self_attention.hpp` formatting/comment tweaks (debug macro comment style and line wrapping) with no functional change.

title: GOF/shard DMA implementation with TRON_SHARD_TEST=1
author: bham0n
head: 2b28a47b1c2467b98e2bc66a66843e605d646866
body:
Introduces a new path for writing K/V data into FPGA HBM using group-of-four (GOF) blocks. Tokens are accumulated into 4-token `gof_buffers`, promoted to immutable `completed_gofs` on completion (zero-copy swap), then DMA'd to HBM. The new path is gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST` env var — when unset, the existing `save_k/v_to_hardware` path is used.



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it adds a new hardware KV DMA write path (including completion polling and blocking gates) and extends token-tree edge split/coalesce logic to preserve new GOF/shard state, which could impact correctness and concurrency in scheduling and HW attention dispatch.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new *experimental* GOF/shard-based KV-to-HBM transfer pipeline gated by `TRON_SHARD_TEST`, accumulating K/V into 4-token `gof_buffer`s, promoting them to immutable `completed_gof`s (zero-copy swap), and DMAing them to device HBM with optional partial-token flushes before GOF completion.
> 
> Introduces `device_dma_tracker` to track per-device in-flight DMA and expose `poll_completions()` plus `await_layer()`; wires this into the scheduler/model loop via new observer hooks (`on_forward_poll`, `on_await_dma`, `on_flush_partial`) and extends `save_k`/`save_v` observers to receive a `node_base*` hint.
> 
> Extends the token-tree (`node_base` + `parent_edge`) to store shards, completed GOFs, embryonic GOFs, and per-session `handle_id`, and updates edge split/coalesce paths to correctly move/merge this new state; adds an FPGA test (`t_gof_dma`) and build plumbing for the new sources.
>

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches low-level DMA completion and wait-loop timing logic; mistakes could cause premature completion or missed timeouts under wrap/counter/CPU-anomaly scenarios.

title: Replace hwkv allocation with shard
author: bham0n
head: 429249ead6170030e2436487914e9b4e0abdc876
body:
This is a follow-on PR to PR 2089, which adds GOFs and shards. Here we remove the allocation mechanism that was introduced on hwattention_sync as part of the AOF development effort, which supported only a single model and concurrent user, and switches to the GOF/shard infrastructure.

This is a work in progress, and depends upon PR 2089 merging to hwattention_sync first.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> High risk because it changes how HW attention finds and manages KV cache HBM addresses (moving from a global singleton to per-shard allocations) and touches scheduler/GOF save/flush paths that can affect correctness and performance across layers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Moves HW KV cache ownership from the global `hwkv_rings` singleton to per-`shard` HBM allocations.** Shards now allocate and free per-layer K/V HBM regions (`alloc_kv_weights` + new `free_kv_weights`) and GOF DMA paths write into these shard bases.
> 
> **Wires shard bases into HW attention execution.** `gof_configure` now tracks `max_layers`, embryonic GOF keying switches to `gof_global * n_layers + layer`, and `prepare_and_launch_hw` populates `wqentry::kv_k_base/kv_v_base` via new `gof_kv_bases`, which the FPGA worker uses instead of `get_hwkv()`.
> 
> **Splits and modernizes debug/test utilities.** Large dump/debug helpers are removed from `hwattention.hpp` and reintroduced as shard-aware helpers in new `pos/hwattention_dump.hpp`; multiple tests are updated to allocate their own KV HBM regions and stop relying on deprecated `save_k_to_hardware`/`save_v_to_hardware` and `hwkv_rings` setup.
>

I'm torn if we should get this all merged ASAP to get the revised prepare/fill API layered with it, or if we should get that API into place and then shift this to more fully use the revised API.  @Wado-posi @bham0n  thoughts?

Since this `kv_hint` is going to be removed after the integration with the new scheduler, I'll explain it here:

There has been, since the token tree v2 change, a very consistent mapping of tokens along an edge to their K/V host memory in books (for the software-only implementation). All the tokens along an edge must be contiguously stored within the same book. Furthermore, it follows that splits cause two new edges to be created: one that points to the chunk of tokens after the split point, and the other that points to the divergent token and its successors, which are allocated always from a new book. Coalescing edges joins tokens only if the two sets of tokens are in a contiguous region of the same book. What follows is this corollary: *All the tokens' KV entries within a book correspond to all of the tokens along the edges of a path through the tree*. The node of that path closest to the root is the _rootward_ node, and the one closest to the leaf is the _leafward_ node.

Now, a book only has space for a single back reference to the token tree, so what I have done is defined this `kv_hint` to point to the *most leafward node* of the path containing all the tokens of this book. I enforce this invariant using a mutator for kv_hint (you're not allowed to access this member directly, but you must call a mutator that takes a node_base* as its argument. That mutator will ignore a request to assign if it allready is assigned to a more leafward node in the tree. So only the tokens that cause this mutator to be called from that portion of the book containing those final tokens in the path will "win" and have their value stored.

Now, when we get a callback in `on_save_k` or `on_save_v`, we can deduce the book to which our k or v pointer refers. From there, we can get the `kv_hint`. Now, a call to `canonicalize()` will take this pointer, and the absolute token height (which we also know from the callback parameters) to fix up this pointer by following the kv_hint's parent_ptr until parent_ptr->abs_ht < abs_ht. We also are protected from nodes in the tree disappearing via coalesce operations using a tombstone mechanism that was designed into the token tree; and `canonicalize()` will also fix those references as well!

This hack has a performance cost. Once we have the canonicalized pointer, we now need to traverse leafward from there to find all the shards that a GOF change at the node could impact. 

A better solution is planned, where the scheduler (from a single compute_forward_args call) will make calls back to this code to "open a ticket" to process the token. We will figure out which embryonic GOF should be associated with that ticket, allocating if necessary. So we will end up creating one ticket per GOF. The ticket context will also contain the actual node*, and do the traversal looking for the shards only one time instead of eight. Next, the on_save_[kv] callbacks will pass this ticket context back, eliminating the need for the `kv_hint` hack.

title: Enable pos_shutdown in test listener with DMA cleanup
author: hvaneenoo-positron
head: 5e2d19d3626d679ccd20003a4de46f4975a15373
body:
## Why this change exists

`pos_shutdown()` was commented out in test listeners across the codebase with the note: *"Crashes and burns due to unfreed allocations."* This caused:

1. **Every test binary leaked hugepages and DMA allocations** (tracked in #1733)
2. **Intermittent segfaults in `t_dma`** during process exit (#1535, #2400) — all 3 test cases pass, then the process segfaults during teardown because the kernel tears down VFIO BAR mappings while static destructors still reference them

The root cause: `PosDevice::init()` allocates DMA buffers and queues, but nothing freed them. `pos_shutdown()` was disabled because calling it triggered heap asserts on the outstanding allocations.

## What changed

### DMA cleanup infrastructure
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `PosDevice::destroy()` | Matching free for `init()`. Without it, heap assert fires on shutdown. |
| `hwkv_rings` destructor | Frees 128 cache block DMA allocations. |
| `delete device` + `devices.clear()` in `pos_shutdown` | Without this, device objects leak and restart appends duplicates. |
| Zero-init pointer members in `PosDevice` | `destroy()` null-checks before freeing; uninitialized pointers cause garbage `dma_deallocate`. |
| `pos_heap_active_allocations()` | DMA allocation counter (real heap + fake-mode). Enables leak detection in test listeners. |

### t_dma segfault fix (#1535, #2400)
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Enable `pos_shutdown()` in `TestDmaListener` | Without it, process exit races VFIO BAR teardown against static destructors → segfault. |
| Release DmaQueues in transfer test | Test acquired TX/RX queues per device but never called `release()`. |
| Baseline allocation tracking | Record `pos_heap_active_allocations()` after `pos_startup()`, warn only if tests leak above that baseline. The 288 device-init allocations (64 device.cpp + 64 consumed_head + 32 ring buffers + 128 hwkv_rings) are expected. |

### Restart lifecycle hardening
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `pos_startup()` idempotency guard | Prevents duplicate device scan if called twice without shutdown. |
| `vfio_groups = nullptr` after delete | Prevents double-free on second shutdown. |
| `get_group_fd` EBUSY retry | IOMMU teardown is async; rapid restart cycles hit EBUSY on group reopen. |

### Test + review feedback
| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| `t_pos_restart` (3 FPGA cases) | Restart produces same device count, idempotency, double-shutdown. |
| `t_pos_lifecycle_fake` (6 cases) | Shutdown with outstanding allocs, allocation tracking, reinit. |
| `INFO()` diagnostic in lifecycle test | Per mcherba review — surfaces allocation count on failure. |

## What this does NOT change

Production behavior is unaffected. `pos_shutdown()` was already called at process exit in Rinzler. The only behavioral change is in test infrastructure — listeners now clean up instead of leaking.

### Superseded by main (resolved during merge)
- Inline group init in `vfio_device_init` → main serialized into `vfio_init_groups()` (better race fix)
- `host_initialized` double-call guard → landed independently on main

## Test results

- `make test-host`: 53/53 passed (cloud-atlas-873f)
- `t_dma`: 5/5 clean runs on 8 FPGAs, zero segfaults, zero leak warnings, clean `pos_shutdown()`
- `make format && make lint`: clean

## Test plan

- [x] `make build-test && make test-host` — 53/53 pass
- [x] `t_dma` — 5 consecutive runs, clean shutdown, no segfault
- [ ] `t_pos_restart` (FPGA CI) — restart lifecycle regression tests
- [ ] `t_pos_lifecycle` (FPGA CI) — existing lifecycle tests
- [ ] Full CI matrix (AMD + Intel runners)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches shutdown paths for FPGA/VFIO + DMA heap lifecycles; bugs here can cause use-after-free, leaks, or restart flakiness, but changes are narrowly scoped to cleanup and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Ensures `pos_shutdown()` actually frees **DMA-backed** resources instead of leaking hugepages/VFIO state, enabling safe teardown in tests and repeated `pos_startup()` cycles.
> 
> Adds `PosDevice::destroy()` and defensive member initialization to release DMA queues/buffers and disable mailbox/tracer write targets before BAR/IOMMU teardown; also gives `hwkv_rings` a destructor to free its ring allocations. Introduces `pos_heap_available()`/`pos_heap_active_allocations()` (real + fake) and improves heap shutdown diagnostics.
> 
> Hardens restart behavior by making `pos_startup()` idempotent, fully deleting/clearing device/global state in `pos_shutdown()`, nulling `vfio_groups` after free, and retrying VFIO group open on `EBUSY`. Updates test listeners to warn on DMA leaks, re-enables shutdown in `t_dma` (and releases per-test queues), and adds new lifecycle/restart regression tests (`t_pos_restart`, expanded `t_pos_lifecycle_fake`).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 5e2d19d3626d679ccd20003a4de46f4975a15373. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: TSX-based mwait
author: BillBaumann
head: 83ab8462773be37bd7534f66523688b5fd37fbca
body:
Implement mwaitx using TSX/RTM with tpause.

mwaitx is triggered by touches to the trigger's cache line.

RTM transactions cause the transaction to abort when the trigger's cache line is touched.  The transaction entails a tpause in a rdtsc() loop.  The processor resumes as if the tpause didn't happen.  Meaning immediate wake up.   This is effectively just how mwaitx works. Clever!   (not my idea).

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches core KV-cache save path, scheduler traversal, and HW-attention planning/execution; regressions could break correctness or performance and add subtle concurrency issues (atomic completion tracking, async DMA coordination). Also changes device job interfaces (`fill_attn_job_template`) and join logic across SW/HW paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Implements a **Phase 1/2 HW-attention refactor**: GOFs are consolidated into a new `hardware::gof` with captured `page_info` accessors, and per-query `gof_job` entries are produced by the scheduler traversal and passed to the model as spans for *tree-unaware* `gof_rodeo` DMA dispatch.

> 
> Updates the forward/attention pipeline to use the plan-based HW path: `save_k/save_v` now track per-token KV completion via atomics on pages and trigger `gof_rodeo`; `self_attention` prepares/launches multiple HW passes (multi-Q `fill_attn_job_template` API), merges HW pass scratchpads during joins, and removes the previous HW validation/observer plumbing and `hw_kv_section`-based planning.

author: bham0n
head: d39c222fa8ba2af9bb11858e0cd5d7312858f999
body:
A new unit test, `t_clearhbm` is added (disabled for normal CI runs) which uses an approach developed by @Wado-posi to clear the HBM. This runs on all the devices in the instance in parallel for speed.

On Atlas, with the FPGAs running bitfile `archer_128col_nan_reg.rbf` , I ran the following command after cycling power on the box, waiting for the system to come back online, confirming that platformd finished successfully, then ran the following commands:

```
cd ~/code/tron
export TRON_LOG_LEVEL=info
SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 0,2" gen/t_clearhbm & SYSTEM_CONFIG="--instance 1,2" gen/t_clearhbm & wait
```
Within 15 seconds the command completed successfully. Afterwards, any runtron command run on any card would produce meaningful output (no gibberish, no NaNs). An example of such a command is:
```
gen/runtron --dont-stop --nr_hugepages 48 --seed 42 --model llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast --instance 4,8 --iterations 1 --length 644 --prompt-length 380 -f /scratch/mcherba/democlient_prompts/llama_test_prompts/prompts_512/pg2349.txt
```
The `t_clearhbm` executable can potentially be used as a temporary workaround that can be run immediately after a power cycle, platformd start, to eliminate that initial "bad state" which is present in the latest bitfile.

title: Merge golden gof/shard implementations (Claude vs Gemini.
author: BillBaumann
head: 4666560ff1349fe7f8c86173de03a015c26f2ba3
body:
Implements golden-gof-shard.md design by merging the best parts of two independent implementations:

- gal struct as authoritative GOF store (unique_ptr on edges)
- Query-driven gal creation with page_info on gal
- Trailing boundary shard creation logic
- Ascent-based shards_getting_gofs propagation
- Shard push filtering with hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload threshold
- DMA tracker clear() + bounds assertions
- Comprehensive phase1-5 integration tests

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches scheduler traversal, HW KV offload eligibility, and DMA/backfill paths, so mistakes could cause incorrect attention results or missed offloads. Changes are contained to the GOF/shard offload pipeline and are covered by expanded integration tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces per-edge GOF storage with an edge-owned **authoritative `gal` (GOF-for-all-layers) repository**, where each `gof_job` points at a `gal` holding the shared `page_info` and per-layer GOFs.
> 
> Updates the scheduler’s GOF/shard pipeline to be *query-driven*: `gal` objects are created only when a query token completes a GOF, shards needing the GOF are determined on ascent (`shards_getting_gofs`), and `gof_rodeo_impl` now DMAs only to shards whose token ranges cover the GOF position.
> 
> Reworks shard management by creating shards via **trailing-boundary logic**, adding shard offload eligibility filtering (including `hwkv_min_gofs_for_offload` and partial-shard handling), and making DMA tracking more robust via `device_dma_tracker::clear()`, bounds assertions, and reset/shutdown cleanup. Integration tests are extended to cover the new phases and edge cases.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4666560ff1349fe7f8c86173de03a015c26f2ba3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

### Passing `cfg.max_layers` (-1) instead of `n_layers` to GOF configure **High Severity** The call to `gof_configure` changed from passing `n_layers` (a `static constexpr size_t` with the actual layer count, e.g. 32) to `cfg.max_layers` (an `int` defaulting to -1, meaning "all layers"). When `cfg.max_layers` is -1, the implicit conversion to `size_t` produces a massive value (~2^64-1), which is then truncated to `uint32_t` (4294967295) inside `gof_configure`. This causes downstream code to attempt allocating billions of layers per shard and per gal, leading to catastrophic failures.

title: reduce compiler noise under nix
author: bham0n
head: 514b90e349f17d249c0a2442a02f98ab1390c5b8
body:
## Background
The nix configuration file `flake.nix` specifies the toolchain and all dependencies for the tron repository. A key benefit of nix is the ability to encapsulate the development environment (tools, dependencies) into that configuration file, so that changes in tools/dependencies can be developed and released as regular PRs. Although the CI runners are set up to begin leveraging this capability, at present, they continue to rely on Ansible scripts to maintain consistent native configurations on those hosts.

I have begun to use the `nix develop` shell on my development host, to understand its impact to our work flow; and to identify and fix any problems that we will encounter once the CI hosts switch over.

An early finding was that the Clang v19.1.7 compiler that is available in the `nix develop` shell includes a cc-wrapper that is configured with a slightly more-hardened set of compiler options than the native Ubuntu-packaged clang v19.1.7 compiler. Due to these subtle changes, code that had previously built without warnings is now emitting warnings. This PR resolves the ones that I have been seeing on the `hwattention_sync` branch. 

## Changes
- Check function return values causing warnings in `huge.cpp`, `t_rinzler_{1,2}.cpp`
- Fix `src/pos/dma_queue.cpp`: unnamed `lock_guard` — lock was never actually held

This PR features the same single-commit patch as in PR #2357, rebased onto `hwattention_sync`. That other PR has been closed.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [x] Spot-check `t_rinzler_1` / `t_rinzler_2` run clean



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it changes synchronization in `DmaQueue::acquire` (potentially affecting queue allocation behavior under concurrency) and touches low-level hugepage file truncation handling, though changes are small and mainly add error checking/logging.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Reduces new clang/nix build warnings and fixes a real locking bug.** `DmaQueue::acquire` now stores the `std::lock_guard` in a named variable so the mutex is actually held while selecting/initializing a queue.
> 
> In `huge.cpp`, `ftruncate` failures are now checked and logged instead of ignored, and the Rinzler integration tests explicitly ignore the return value of `system("id > /dev/null")` to silence warnings.

title: t_clearhbm: direct-mode poison + ECC verify (STORY-385)
author: bham0n
head: dfbacb475465bdc11b6992435349080a2008a40b
body:
## Summary

Reworks `t_clearhbm`'s poison mode to write through the WIM/RIM (9/8) window instead of the Bypass (8/8) window, so the source buffer bytes land in both data and ECC regions of each 576-byte `strip`. Adds a verify mode that confirms the write survived via an identity-matmul readback.

Background from STORY-397: the Bypass DMA used by the previous poison path auto-fills scale bytes to bf16(1.0), regardless of source bytes. That mechanistically explains why every previous attempt to reproduce the post-power-cycle defect through `TRON_POISON_BITS` has failed — the ECC bits the defect depends on weren't reachable through that path.

Two commits:
- **`t_clearhbm: call get_devices()`** (latent bug fix, separable): `ClearHbmListener` was calling `pos_startup()` directly, which populates the device mask but skips the per-device TX/RX worker spawn. Any matmul or `set_hardware_weights` call would then spin forever on `tx_worker_ready`. Switch to `get_devices()` which does both atomically. Prerequisite for any matmul work in this test.
- **`t_clearhbm: add direct-mode poison and ECC verify (STORY-385)`**: main change.

## Behavior

Three modes, gated by env vars (composable):
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=0` (default): zeroize mode, unchanged from before.
- `TRON_POISON_BITS=X` nonzero: direct-mode poison. Writes `uint16(X)` repeated into every byte of the full weight-region HBM (all 32 fetchers × 1.125 GiB = 36 GiB per device, parallel across 8 devices), via 9/8 DMA.
- `TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: after the poison pass, run identity-matmul readback and assert every output cell equals `bf16(X) × dequant[low_nibble_of_low_byte(X)]`.

## Scope note

Per project convention, `t_clearhbm` remains a unit test (`DISABLED TRUE` in `t/CMakeLists.txt`, opt-in via `./gen/t_clearhbm`). Promotion to a first-class tool is out of scope.

## Empirical results (STORY-385 FoM)

Ran `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0 ./gen/t_clearhbm` followed by runtron on andoria-06 (`llama-3.1-8b-instruct-fast`, prompt-length 380, length 644):

| Condition                       | Post-power-cycle defect   | Direct-mode poison `0x7fc0`                          |
| ---                             | ---                       | ---                                                  |
| 1st runtron after setup         | Fails with attention NaN  | Fails with attention NaN (`m_star != -inf` assert)   |
| 2nd runtron (no intervening op) | Succeeds (state self-clears) | Fails again (poison persistent)                   |
| Runtron after zeroize           | Succeeds                  | Succeeds                                             |

**Capability achieved:** direct-mode poison puts a card into an attention-NaN state on demand and that state is clearable via the existing zeroize path. Zero false negatives on `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1` (all 32,768 output cells match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit).

**Signature difference from real power-cycle defect:** our direct-mode poison is strictly more aggressive than the real defect. It persists across runtron invocations because it overwrites the full 9/8 window (36 GiB per device), where the real defect is almost certainly a much smaller ECC-state anomaly that any single runtron op overwrites in passing. Because zeroize clears both, the two states share a family of "ECC/scale bytes in a bad configuration."

**Value delivered by this PR:**
- Eliminates the power-cycle step from the FPGA team's debug cycle. Any candidate fix has to survive a test that triggers attention NaN via poison and clears via zeroize, without the multi-minute overhead of a physical power cycle.
- Narrows the defect's home to something the 9/8 window can address and zeroize's bypass-path bf16(1.0) auto-fill can clear.
- Provides a stronger stress test than the power-cycle defect itself (since our poison is wider).

**Finding a surgical pattern** that reproduces the power-cycle defect's exact fail-once-pass-after signature is a separate empirical search — tracked under STORY-395 (bisection modes) for systematic exploration, or via FPGA-team input on what the post-power-cycle ECC state actually is.

## Coverage caveat

The `reserved[16]` field of each `strip` (32 bytes of ECC region per strip) is not consumed by the systolic, so verify cannot observe it. If the defect pattern turns out to live specifically in `reserved`, a different observation mechanism is needed — out of scope for this PR, tracked under STORY-396.

## Test plan

- [x] `make gen/t_clearhbm` — clean build
- [x] `make format` — no changes needed
- [x] `make lint` — clean
- [x] `make build-test` — clean (verified by author)
- [x] Zeroize sanity (no env vars): all 9 Catch2 assertions pass on andoria-06
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x4444 TRON_VERIFY_ECC=1`: all 32,768 output cells (4096 × 8) match expected `0x4544` bit-for-bit, exit 0
- [x] `TRON_POISON_BITS=0x7fc0` followed by runtron: **runtron fails with attention NaN on first invocation**, confirming direct-mode poison successfully induces a defective attention state
- [x] Zeroize + runtron: **runtron succeeds post-zeroize**, confirming recovery

## Related stories

- [STORY-385](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/344d132d3cfd8167abe6d39d5940edc3) (this PR)
- [STORY-397](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd8185af3ff95f3692454c) (done): characterization that showed bypass DMA auto-fills ECC to bf16(1.0)
- [STORY-396](https://www.notion.so/positron-ai/346d132d3cfd813ebe14c5e57d6caa06) (deferred): reading un-written HBM requires FPGA-team input
- STORY-395 (blocked on 385): bisection modes for FPGA team debugging

title: resolve minibatch race in GOF firing
author: bham0n
head: 1b728fbfad0e447d9d30fadcab58f3cb3cbc56ef
body:
When running `gen/t_generate_2` at "tp1" (all eight FPGA devices claimed), a `TRON_ASSERT` fires in fire_gof_rodeo (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1597): "GOF rodeo for job 17 but token at pos 348 not kv_complete at layer 0"

The problem is that in TP1, the minibatch size is sometimes not a multiple of 4, which produces a situation where the downstream minibatch can fire the GOF before the upstream has finished writing the mates' K/V.

The fix provided here:

Replace the firing-token-only predicate `(pos+1)%gof_tokens==0 && k_completing` with a per-GOF, per-layer atomic `save_count` on `tron::hardware::gof`. Every `save_k`/`save_v` on a GOF participant — firing token or non-firing mate — does `fetch_add(1, acq_rel)`; the increment that reaches `2*gof_tokens` (8) fires `gof_rodeo`. At gal construction, mates already kv_complete from prior forwards (or non-query mates without saves coming) are pre-loaded by 2. The scheduler also replicates the firing slot's `gof_jobs[]` entry into each non-firing query mate's job_id, so any mate's save can fire and `gof_rodeo_impl` produces identical work via shared `gal_ptr`/`tok_position`/`shards_getting_gofs`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**

title: Scope GOF mate replication to this edge's flat-array range
author: bham0n
head: e3e7903a45503f79f27f735a84a064f0874a338e
body:
## Problem

`t_scheduler` and `t_generate_2` were tripping a kv_complete assertion in `fire_gof_rodeo`:

```
TRON_ASSERT(job.gal_ptr->pages[p].kv_complete_fn(layer)):
  GOF rodeo for job 3 but token at pos 2 not kv_complete at layer 0
```

The GOF mate replication loop in `full_scheduler` matched mates by abs position alone, picking the first `token_jobs` entry whose `token_positions` equals `mate_pos`. With branching, two edges can produce gals at the same gof position; the unfiltered match assigned the same `tok_id` to both gals' `gof_jobs` slots, and the later replication overwrote the earlier. `save_k`/`save_v` then incremented the wrong gal's `save_count`, the count hit 8, the rodeo fired, and the gal read its own pages — which the saves had never touched (`kv_saves=0`). Hence the assertion.

Concretely, in the failing run: a gal at `gof_pos=3` belonging to a branch edge (`edge_base=2`, `edge_start_idx=55`) captured `pages[2,3]` from its own `kv_book` (`0x...10b980`/0,1), but the saves for `tok_id=2,3` came from the *root* edge writing to `0x...15bb00`/2,3.

This regression is on `ff35fc684`, not `1224520e7` (mcherba's hwattention sync change).

## Solution

Restrict the replication search to tok_ids in `[edge_start_idx, edge_start_idx + edge.token_count())` so each gal accumulates `save_count` only from its own edge's saves. Mates without an in-edge save target fall through to the existing preload path.

## Test plan

- [x] `gen/t_scheduler` — 4 clean runs (was failing every run pre-fix)
- [x] `gen/t_generate_2` — 2 clean runs
- [x] `make lint`

title: src/tron: heap-allocate token_cache singleton
author: BillBaumann
head: 6f05f725d49bb341704d13b376b77e9b96678948
body:
## Summary

The `token_cache()` singleton is a `static token_cache_t it`, which means it gets destroyed during static destruction. Other globals reference it during their own destruction, leading to use-after-destroy races at process exit.

This PR switches the singleton to `static token_cache_t* it = new ...; return *it;` — intentional leak, defers destruction to OS exit. No behavioral change at runtime; only fixes shutdown.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target t_token_cache` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

Originally authored by: Wado-posi

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: change only affects process-shutdown lifetime semantics by intentionally leaking the singleton; normal runtime behavior should remain unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents exit-time use-after-destruction by changing `token_cache()` from a function-local `static token_cache_t` to a heap-allocated singleton (`static token_cache_t*`), so it is not destroyed during global/static teardown.
> 
> This is an intentional leak to avoid other globals (e.g., scheduler shutdown paths) touching `token_cache` after its destructor would have run.
>

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the HW attention GOF backfill path and changes when data is DMA’d, which can impact correctness and HW/SW boundary behavior despite being a small diff.
> 
> **Overview**
> Tightens `backfill_shard` to **only DMA/backfill GOFs that are fully saved**, by gating on `g->save_count >= 2 * gof_tokens` before populating and transferring.

title: h/tron: add GoF/Shard core type headers
author: BillBaumann
head: 4cc4ceb572a5f81b6ba88a93cd719096c7113f63
body:
## Summary

Adds the foundational hardware-attention type *declarations* — `gof.hpp` and `shard.hpp` — that the upcoming hardware-attention work will build on. Headers only, no implementation. Build-clean: nothing on main includes them yet, so they compile to nothing.

- `h/tron/gof.hpp`: GOF (group-of-four) types — `page_info`, `gof`, `gal`, `gof_job`, plus the `gof_rodeo_fn_t` typedef and `backfill_shard` declaration. The header reflects the post-redesign API: per-shard `hw_attn_params const* hw_params` rather than module-scope state.
- `h/tron/shard.hpp`: `shard` type for HW KV cache management. The ctor takes `hw_attn_params const*` (defaulted to `nullptr` for test stubs with `max_layers == 0`).

Some function declarations (e.g., `gof::populate`, `backfill_shard`) reference symbols not yet on main. As long as nothing calls those functions, the link stage is happy. Implementations land in a follow-up PR alongside the supporting infrastructure (`device_dma_tracker`, `HW_MAX_KV_HEADS` / `hwkv_max_layers` constants, the `hw_attn_params` extension).

The `POS_PER_PAGE` rename from hwattention_sync is held back to `pos_per_page` to match main's current spelling; this aligns automatically with the future PR that brings `pos/hwattention.hpp`'s broader rename.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [ ] CI green

Originally authored by: Brian Hamon, Mike Cherba, Wado-posi

title: h/tron/models/kv_cache: per-token KV completion counters
author: BillBaumann
head: 8f6b76bad96b8a0c22066995fd319adeaf6c6677
body:
## Summary

Adds per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking to `tron::page`. New atomic
counter `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` (`std::atomic<uint8_t>[page_size][n_layers]`)
records how many of {K, V} have been saved for each (offset, layer); the call
that pushes the count to 2 is the completing save. Comes with the helpers
`mark_k_complete` / `mark_v_complete` (fetch_add(1, acq_rel), return true on
completion), `is_kv_complete` (acquire load >= 2), and `clear_kv_complete_at`
(relaxed reset across all layers, intended to be called when a new token is
assigned to a page offset).

Two new public accessors for direct V-buffer extraction ride along here:
`v_ptr(layer, kv_head, i_page)` on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16` path returns
a raw bf16 pointer into the page, and a new
`get_v(layer, kv_head, i_page, bf16*)` overload on the `TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16`
path uninterleaves the striped bf16 storage into a contiguous bf16 buffer.
They have nothing to do with the completion counters; they're called later
by `gof::populate` / `backfill_shard` ([PR #2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695)).
They land in this PR because removing them would make this file deviate from
hwattention_sync, and #2695 would then have to add them back.

`page`'s move constructor is replaced with an explicit one because
`std::atomic` is not movable; it copies the loaded counter values
element-by-element with relaxed ordering and is only invoked during
single-threaded vector construction. A forward declaration of
`struct node_base;` is also added ahead of the `tron` namespace contents
for use by future callers.

This feature is **inert** until callers wire it in (#2695 onward). No build
without HW attention is affected, and no existing call site changes.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run -Werror clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

## Notes for reviewers

The forward declaration `struct node_base;` is unused in this header today;
later code (Future AoF merge PRs) includes this header and references the type. 
Landing it now keeps the per-PR diffs minimal.

Originally authored by: Wado-posi, Brian Hamon

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces new per-token/per-layer atomic counters and a custom move constructor in `tron::page`, which affects concurrency behavior and object movement in a performance-critical KV cache path. Also extends AVX512 `V` access APIs; incorrect use could lead to subtle correctness/perf issues.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **per-token, per-layer KV completion tracking** to `tron::page` via a new `kv_saves_[offset][layer]` atomic counter and helper APIs (`mark_k_complete`, `mark_v_complete`, `is_kv_complete`, `clear_kv_complete_at`) intended to let callers trigger work once both K and V are saved.
> 
> Updates `page` move semantics to an explicit move constructor that copies atomic counter values, and extends V-buffer access by adding `v_ptr(...)` on the non-interleaved path and a new AVX512 `get_v(..., bf16*)` overload to uninterleave stored V data into a contiguous bf16 buffer.
>

title: h/tron/models/ranged_mask: use real shard type; push-time DMA filter
author: BillBaumann
head: 0164131e16a0f8a79a462dedabfa4353c769802a
body:
## Summary

Three coordinated changes to `ranged_mask`, plus two explanatory comments added in response to CQA review:

- **`h/tron/models/ranged_mask.hpp`** drops the stub `shard` struct in favour of `using shard = tron::hardware::shard;` — the real type lands via [#2676](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2676).
- **`src/tron/models/ranged_mask.cpp`** has two surgical fixes plus two explanatory comments:
  - Push-time cursor fix: the shard pop now uses `< hi` instead of `< edge_hi`, matching the loop comment.
  - Pop-time `dma_complete` gate is removed.
  - New comment above the `have_shard`/`have_query` guards explains why the shard guard uses the shrinking `hi` while the query guard keeps `edge_hi` (prior pop_backs already trim the query stack to match — both reach the same trim).
  - New comment in the SW→HW transition block notes that DMA-complete eligibility is enforced at push time by the walker (`h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp`), so the unconditional pop here relies on a caller guarantee.
- **`t/t_ranged_mask.cpp`** swaps the stub `b_shard` aggregate initializer for `shard(nullptr, 0, 0)` (the real shard has a deleted copy ctor; `max_layers=0` is the test-stub sentinel that makes `dma_complete()` true).

Why now: [#2676](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2676)'s headers provide the real shard type, so the local stub becomes redundant. The `dma_complete` eligibility filter is moving from pop-time to push-time — a follow-up walker PR will only push DMA-complete shards onto the shard stack, so the pop-time gate has no work left to do.

## Test plan

> **Note:** `make test` for this PR fails to link `t_ranged_mask` because the symbols `tron::hardware::shard::shard(...)` and `~shard()` are defined in [#2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695)'s `src/tron/gof.cpp`. Static-lib (`tron`) builds clean. Full link/test verification deferred until [#2695](https://github.com/positron-ai/tron/pull/2695) lands.


- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

## Notes for reviewers

1. **Doc drift** (`doc/hw-kv-rules.md:15-18, 64, 82`): describes shard offloadability with the old pop-time check semantics. Out of scope for this PR; flag for follow-up.

2. The `using shard = tron::hardware::shard;` alias exposes `tron::hardware::shard` (DMA state, HBM ownership) into the `tron::` namespace via header transitivity. Not a defect; coupling note.

Originally authored by: Mike Cherba, Wado-posi

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when SW queries move to HW masks and fixes shard-event ordering in range building—incorrect bounds or eligibility would mis-route attention work.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Ranged mask** now uses **`tron::hardware::shard`** instead of a local stub, with **`edge_shard_info`** documented as coming from **`edge.shards[]`**.
> 
> In **`build_edge_ranges`**, the shard-event guard compares against the loop’s shrinking **`hi`** (not **`edge_hi`**), aligning shard pops with the documented “highest event in [edge_lo, hi)” behavior. **SW→HW transitions** on shard pop no longer check **`dma_complete()`**; offload is assumed only for shards the walker already pushed as DMA-ready (filter moving to **`h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp`**).
> 
> Tests construct a real **`shard(nullptr, 0, 0)`** so **`dma_complete()`** is true via **`max_layers == 0`**.
> 
> Also adds **`fwd_hw_attn_enabled()`** in **`hw_attn_config.hpp`** ( **`USE_HW_ATTN`** env, default off).
>

title: src/tron + h/pos: GoF/Shard implementation + device_dma_tracker + pos infra
author: BillBaumann
head: ddd2f0b461c6389bc210fd15a7f463ae48d179a2
body:
# WILL BE CLOSED SOON -- superceded by PR #2796

## Summary

Long-pole implementation drop for the GoF/Shard merge. Lands
`src/tron/gof.cpp` (shard ctor/`xfer_gof`, `gof::populate`) plus the
pos-side infrastructure it depends on. 18 files, organized in two
layers:

- **Layer 1 — h/ infrastructure**: `h/libpos.hpp`, `h/pos/config.hpp`,
  `h/pos/device.hpp`, `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp`, `h/pos/hwattention.hpp`,
  and new `h/pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp` — extends `hw_attn_params`,
  introduces `dma_xfer_state`, virtualizes `xfer`/`xfer_blocking`/
  `isdone`/`wait` on cacheblocks, adds the `device_dma_tracker`
  singleton.
- **Layer 2 — src/ implementation**: new `src/tron/gof.cpp` and
  `src/pos/device_dma_tracker.cpp`; updates to
  `src/pos/{hwattention,driver,device,dma,dma_queue,fake}.cpp`
  matching the header changes; 1-line CMake add for `gof.cpp`.
- **Tests**: `t/t_dma.cpp`, `t/t_mwaitx.cpp` — call-site updates for
  the new `dma_xfer_state` return type from `xfer_blocks`.

## Stub note

`gof::backfill_shard` is intentionally a no-op in this PR (empty body,
parameters commented out, `TODO` comment). The full implementation
walks the scheduler tree via `node_base::tree_parent` /
`tree_height` / `tree_edge_gals` — APIs added in a separate later
patch. No caller in this PR's scope reaches `backfill_shard` (its
only invoker lives in code that depends on those node_base virtuals
that don't exist on main yet). The function declaration in the
already-merged `h/tron/gof.hpp` matches.

## Debug-flag scrub & cleanup (applied during review)

`src/pos/device.cpp` previously had `#define DEBUG_INIT 1` plus
`#ifdef DEBUG_INIT`. Because the macro is always defined, the
`#ifdef` guard was unconditionally true regardless of value — the
debug code was active in every build. Fixed two ways: value flipped
`1` to `0`, and guard changed to `#if DEBUG_INIT` so the value
actually gates compilation. The neighbouring `DEBUG_RESETS` /
`DEBUG_VFIO` macros were converted to the same `#define X 0` + `#if X`
form for consistency.

Two debug-only value bumps that landed in the source branch were
reverted here so they do not propagate to main:

- `maxpolls`: back to `1e9 / timeout_ns` (~1 second), was 100×.
- `max_xfer_time_in_ns`: back to `100000000` (100 ms), was 10 s.

Other small cleanups applied during review:
- Five commented-out `wqentry` fields removed from the public
  `h/pos/device.hpp` struct.
- Three `#if 0` / commented blocks removed from `src/pos/device.cpp`
  (pseudochannel debug print, init register dump, three
  `wcmd/acmd/mdwd` req-id allocations).
- Bounds-check assert added on
  `device_dma_tracker::await_layer`'s `layer` arg, mirroring `push()`.
- Unused `nlohmann_json` link dropped from `pos` and `pos_fake`.
- TODO comment on `fake_devices` null-deref hazard.
- Move-ctor / move-assignment comments on `DmaQueue` extended to state
  the quiescence invariant the relaxed atomic loads rely on.
- One-line comment on `t/t_dma.cpp`'s `kv_xfer = true` to record why
  the kv path is the right one to exercise post-refactor.

## File-level port decisions

Six `h/` files were ported at file level from the source branch rather
than merged surgically:

- `h/libpos.hpp` — `hw_attn_params` extension touches struct layout
  pervasively; piecemeal merge fragile
- `h/pos/device.hpp` — `wqentry` extensions + `dma_xfer_state` struct
  + several constants intertwined
- `h/pos/dma/queue.hpp` — atomic state + move semantics + mutex
  introduce coupled changes throughout the class
- `h/pos/hwattention.hpp` — virtualization of cacheblock xfer API
  cuts across many methods
- `h/pos/device_dma_tracker.hpp` — new file
- (`src/pos/hwattention.cpp` + `src/pos/driver.cpp` + `src/pos/fake.cpp`
  also ported at file level on the cpp side for symmetry — they implement
  the file-level-ported headers)

`h/pos/config.hpp` is surgical (constants only); `src/tron/CMakeLists.txt`
is a 1-line add (`gof.cpp`); the rest of the `src/pos/*.cpp` and the
two test files are surgical.

## Test plan

- [x] clang-format-19 --dry-run clean
- [x] no trailing whitespace vs origin/main
- [x] no new `#include <cassert>`
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target tron` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target pos` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen --target pos_fake` succeeds locally
- [x] `cmake --build gen` (full 665-target build) succeeds locally
- [ ] CI green

Originally authored by: Mike Cherba, Alexey Radul, Wado-posi, Edward Kmett, Brian Hamon, Fritz Obermeyer, Hannah Van Eenoo

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches low-level POS driver DMA submission/completion logic and hardware-attention KV memory layout/transfer paths; concurrency and correctness issues could cause hangs, data corruption, or hard-to-debug device timeouts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a first cut of the **GOF/shard hardware-attention KV offload pipeline** (`src/tron/gof.cpp`): shards allocate per-layer K/V HBM regions (with per-layer HW eligibility via `hw_attn_params::hw_layers`), GOFs populate `k_hwcacheblock`/`v_hwcacheblock`, and `shard::xfer_gof` DMAs those cacheblocks to the device.
> 
> Refactors POS DMA and HW-attention transfer plumbing around a new `dma_xfer_state` token: `xfer_blocks()` now returns structured completion state (descriptor index + wrap count + optional readback), `wait_for_xfer_blocks()` consumes it, and a new `device_dma_tracker` singleton tracks/polls per-device in-flight GOF DMAs and can await per-layer completion.
> 
> Updates HW-attention cacheblock APIs to be **polymorphic** (`hwcacheblock::xfer`/`xfer_blocking` + `isdone`/`wait`), adds padded shuffle support for model `kv_head_size` differing from the bitfile’s baked `HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`, and adjusts attention job templating to support per-batch token indices plus per-shard HBM bases.
> 
> Improves robustness/debuggability in the device/driver layer (larger command FIFO depth, queue producer mutex + wrap tracking, expanded device/queue debug dumps, init/debug flag gating), adds `free_kv_weights()`, and updates tests/cmake/fake builds to the new DMA interfaces.
>

### V-entry readback uses compile-time constant instead of runtime value **Medium Severity** In `xfer_v_entry`, the readback check is gated on `pdc == FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE - 1` (compile-time constant 31), but the loop iterates using `dev->num_fetchers`. If `dev->num_fetchers` differs from `FETCHERS_PER_DEVICE`, the condition is never true and readback verification is silently skipped for every transfer. The sister function `v_hwcacheblock::xfer()` in `hwattention.cpp` correctly uses `pdc == dev->num_fetchers - 1`.

+// Note [Model vs HW head_size]
+// ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+// `kv_head_size` is the model's per-head element count (e.g. 128 for Llama,
+// 64 for GPT-OSS). It drives the systolic working width via `ah_kvh_size`
+// and the logical contract of the attention dot product.
+//
+// `HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE` is the per-head cell count of the deployed bitfile's HBM
+// and W-MEM layout. When the bitfile and model use the same head_size the two are
+// equal and no padding happens. When they differ (e.g. running GPT-OSS
+// head_size=64 on a head_size=128 bitfile) the upper cells are zero-padded and
+// the systolic, programmed from `kv_head_size`, ignores them.
+//
+// `hw_layers` is a per-layer flag indicating which layers are eligible for
+// HW attention (size = max_layers). Layers with `hw_layers[l] == false`
+// are SW-only; their per-shard HBM region is not allocated and HW-side
+// dispatch must skip them. An empty vector means "all layers run on HW",
+// which preserves legacy single-head-size models that never declared the
+// mask.
